sample_size.notes: Sample covers 4 variants (UA/UD x Bull/Bear). Descending scallop has a falling left side.

target_calculation.description: Compute scallop height; project from breakout point in breakout direction.

ultimate_high_method.definition: Highest price after upward breakout before 20% reversal

ultimate_low_method.definition: Lowest price after downward breakout before 20% reversal

failure_definition.description: Break-even failure: price fails to move 5% in breakout direction.

post_breakout_measurement.lookahead_note: Median ~59 days. Descending scallops are FASTER than ascending (shorter time to ultimate).

performance_statistics.best_performer: bear/UD (23% decline, only 8% BE failure — strong bearish continuation)
performance_statistics.worst_performer: bull/UA (22% BE failure — upward breakout of descending scallop in bull market is weak)

notes: PDF source: Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (2nd ed.), chapter 39, p677-706.
Legacy digitized file scallop_ascending_descending_digitized.json groups all 4 scallop variants together with NO failure_rate / sample_size — this file fills that gap for Descending variants.
Critical: descending scallops in BEAR market with DOWNWARD breakout (bear/UD) are the MOST RELIABLE (8% BE failure, 23% decline) — this is a bearish continuation pattern.
Inverted variants (mirror image about horizontal axis) exist but Bulkowski groups them under same statistics — UA/UD variant captures them.
